title: ProofWorkshop onboarding checklist and approval hub — PRD (draft)
content:
Status: draft — brainstorming + onboarding checklist for a small-scope MVP.

Context / motivation:
- Customers running Private (VPC / on-prem) want a low-friction way to onboard networking changes while preserving compact forensic evidence and keeping operator burden low.
- Current PRDs focus on attestation bundles and sampling; this doc sketches a complementary UX-first surface we call "ProofWorkshop" — an evidence-curation and approval hub that turns raw telemetry into human-reviewable summaries and compact receipts for audit.

High-level idea (one-liner):
ProofWorkshop collects pre/post snapshots and associated telemetry for a customer-managed network change, synthesizes a short machine summary and a condensed evidence bundle, and surfaces an approval queue for reviewers with risk signals and suggested gates.

Primary goals for MVP:
- Reduce time-to-approve for routine VPC/operator changes by 40% via summarized evidence and suggested approval policy matches.
- Create a compact, signed evidence bundle (<= 200KB typical) that customers can store or forward to their SIEM.
- Provide an approval hub that supports: single-step approve/deny, batch approve (multi-change), and a lightweight escalation link to full forensic package retrieval.

Key personas:
- Cust Operator (primary): initiates change, needs predictable onboarding, wants minimal back-and-forth with vendor ops.
- Cust Security Reviewer (secondary): triages risk, wants concise summary + link to deep forensic later.
- Redwood Support/SE (internal): occasionally reviews changes, needs audit trails and quick lookups.

User journeys (MVP):
1) Operator initiates change (API / CLI / Portal) -> ProofWorkshop auto-captures: pre-change routing table snapshot, firewall ruleset diff, handshake logs, and a small telemetry slice (first/last 30s).
2) System generates: a short NLP summary (3–6 bullets), a risk score (low/med/high), a compact evidence bundle (signed), and a human-facing digest in the Approval Hub.
3) Reviewer sees digest, risk rationale, and a suggested gate (auto-approve for low-risk SLA customers, require 2nd sign-off for high-risk).
4) Approve action emits an immutable approval receipt (HMAC + timestamp + signer metadata) that can be attached to the change event in the customer’s change log.

What makes this different from existing work in repo:
- Focus on UX that compresses evidence for rapid human triage rather than exhaustive telemetry export.
- ML summarizer + suggested gating policy derived from historical approvals (learning to suggest approvals for routine patterns).
- Tight integration with customer-managed network onboarding flows (handshake + snapshot + signed bundle).

MVP feature list (scoped):
- Auto-capture hooks for: route table diff, security group/firewall diff, NAT/egress rules, control-plane attestation header, basic syslog slice.
- Evidence bundler: canonical JSON manifest + tarball of minimal files → then GZIP + sign (KMS/HSM).
- NLP summarizer: extract 3–6 bullet summary + explicit list of changed resources. Tunable verbosity.
- Approval Hub UI: list view, single-change detail view, batch select + approve, comment field, export receipt button.
- Risk scoring: heuristic first pass (source IP sensitivity, production tag, change size) plus flag for previously-seen change patterns.
- Audit API endpoints: POST /proofworkshop/changes, GET /proofworkshop/{id}/bundle, POST /proofworkshop/{id}/approve

Data model (compact representation):
- change_id: string (UUID)
- initiator: email
- change_manifest: comma-delimited short resource list (string)
- summary: 3–6 bullet plain text
- risk_label: low|medium|high
- evidence_bundle_url: presigned URL
- approval_receipt: base64 signed blob (signed by Redwood KMS; contains signer, timestamp, decision)
(Implementation note: keep manifest fields small; bundle hosts full payload in S3-like object storage with retention TTL.)

Security and tamper-proofing:
- Evidence bundles are signed server-side with customer-anchored key (for Private, option to use customer KMS or Redwood ephemeral key with customer escrow).
- Approval receipts include an immutable audit hash (sha256 of bundle + decision) and are appended to the customer change record.
- Minimal PII: scrub hostnames / replace with hashes unless customer opts in.

Onboarding checklist for pilot (operational steps):
- [ ] Wire a capture hook in customer onboarding script (pre-change snapshot + post-change snapshot). Link: onboarding script stub in repo.
- [ ] Add small syslog-forward rule (sample) to include initial handshake logs.
- [ ] Enable ProofWorkshop feature flag for pilot account.
- [ ] Seed a small ruleset for risk heuristics (prod-tags, critical-subnets).
- [ ] Create one templated approval policy for pilot (auto-approve: low-risk non-prod; require-2: any change touching protected subnets).
- [ ] Configure KMS choice: customer KMS or Redwood-managed escrow.
- [ ] Run 3 synthetic onboarding changes and validate signed receipts are verifiable.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Evidence bundle size median <= 200KB for pilot changes.
- NLP summary present and captures the changed resource names in >90% of cases in a small test corpus.
- Approval action writes a verifiable receipt and the customer change log shows the receipt hash.
- UI lists changes with correct risk labels for a seeded dataset (manual verification).

Rollout plan (phases):
- Pilot (1–2 customers): enable feature flag, close support loop with SE on first 10 changes. (2 weeks)
- Beta (10 customers): collect acceptance metrics, begin ML summarizer tuning with customer-provided labeled approvals. (6 weeks)
- GA: integrated into Private onboarding flow and exposed as optional toggle in Console.

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes to team):
- To what extent do customers want raw forensic access vs. compact bundles? We should support both, but default to compact to minimize storage & IR noise.
- ML summarizer risk: hallucination of resources — we need conservative extraction fallback that always lists machine-extracted resource names first.
- Retention: default short retention (30d) for bundle store + allow export to customer archive. Cost implications for S3 storage TBD.
- Customer KMS integration timeline — if late, default to Redwood-managed signing with clear product limitations documented.

Edge cases and failure modes:
- Bundle signing failure: fallback to unsigned bundle with a clearly marked warning + manual approval path.
- Snapshot capture fails mid-change: mark evidence as partial and require additional human validation (UI shows missing pieces).
- High-risk change with auto-approve suggested due to skewed heuristics: require a manual override/2nd signer and log model suggestion provenance.

Measurement / telemetry for product ops:
- Approval latency (time from change creation -> decision). Target: reduce by 40% vs baseline.
- Bundle size distribution and retention cost.
- False suggestion rate for auto-approve (monitor suggestions accepted vs rejected).
- Number of escalations to full forensic retrieval.

Implementation notes for Eng teams (rough):
- Capture hooks can reuse existing network-onboard probes but should write to the new proofworkshop staging bucket.
- NLP summarizer can initially be a light deterministic extractor (resource name regexes + top-line template) with a future lift to small LLM summarizer in sandbox.
- Approval receipts stored in audit DB (immutable append-only table); provide a verification endpoint for customers that verifies receipt signature + hash.

Stakeholder requests to fold in if possible: 
- CS: add an export button (PDF) for customers who need human-readable evidence for compliance reviews.
- SRE: include a debug endpoint to fetch raw captured artifacts for fast incident triage.
- Security: include HSM-backed signing path as an opt-in for high-compliance customers.

Next steps (immediate):
- Product: refine acceptance criteria and finalize pilot customers (Aisha + Liam to own).
- Eng: spike on bundler + signing flow (Noor + Ravi). Deliver prototype by 2026-01-15.
- Design: quick mockups of Approval Hub list/detail views (Sofia lead) by 2025-11-01.

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Draft a short internal playbook for Support to interpret receipts.
- Add a small test corpus of 30 synthetic change events in repo for testing summarizer heuristics.
- Add a short FAQ for customers about what the bundle contains and how to verify.

----
Revision history (quick):
- 2025-10-18: initial concept note (Aisha).
- 2025-12-12: added onboarding checklist and data model (Liam).
- 2026-03-01: tuned acceptance criteria, added rollout phases and implementation notes (Aisha).

Questions for reviewers (please reply inline):
- Should proof bundles default to including trimmed packet-level metadata? pros/cons.
- Do we want to allow customers to attach their own policy templates during onboarding? (I think yes for pilot).

End of draft.
